themes_detail.label: Mysterious SPIT Inspection Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, a 2700% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.2 complaints per week (z-score: 15.59), suggesting either a sudden enforcement campaign or an unidentified structural/safety issue affecting multiple properties in Fordham/University Heights.
evidence: 7 SPIT complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 15.59 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No prior pattern of SPIT complaints in district suggests sudden trigger
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development to understand what triggered SPIT deployment this week and which buildings are affected
Interview residents at properties under SPIT inspection to understand what violations prompted complaints

themes_detail.label: Lead Contamination Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead-related 311 complaints jumped to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1900% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.2 per week (z-score: 10.97), indicating possible lead exposure concerns in aging housing stock or drinking water in this older Bronx neighborhood.
evidence: 5 lead complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.97 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Community Board repeatedly requests air quality and public health investigations (recurring budget request)
reporting_angles: Identify which specific addresses reported lead concerns and whether they are school buildings, residential buildings, or water infrastructure
Interview NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene about whether they detected lead in water or paint at those locations and what remediation is underway
Interview families with young children in affected buildings about testing and health screening access

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation-related 311 complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 471% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week (z-score: 6.88), potentially signaling a water main break, pressure loss, or city-mandated conservation enforcement in the district.
evidence: 5 water conservation complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Concurrent with water leak complaints DOWN 74% this week (14 vs. 54.1 avg), possibly indicating infrastructure intervention
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if a water main break or emergency repairs occurred 2 weeks ago in Fordham/University Heights
Check DEP water quality reports for the district during the spike period

themes_detail.label: Homelessness & Assistance Requests Rising
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 211% increase from the 8-week baseline of 2.2 per week (z-score: 4.36), reflecting possible clustering of unsheltered individuals or a visible encampment in the Fordham/University Heights area.
evidence: 7 homeless assistance complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Community Board requests multiple programs to address public health issues (recurring request suggesting ongoing advocacy)
reporting_angles: Scout Fordham Road, Grand Concourse, and transit hubs for visible encampments or clusters of unsheltered individuals
Interview local service providers (Dattran Community Center, local nonprofits) about recent upticks in need or shelter capacity issues

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints rose to 6 LAST WEEK, a 220% increase from the 8-week baseline of 1.9 per week (z-score: 3.54), suggesting concentrated sidewalk damage or pothole formation in specific blocks of the district, possibly linked to recent weather or infrastructure failure.
evidence: 6 sidewalk condition complaints filed last week vs. 1.9 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Community Board repeatedly requests increased sanitation trucks and equipment, suggesting chronic street maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Request specific sidewalk complaint addresses from 311 data and physically verify conditions on highest-complaint blocks
Contact NYC Department of Transportation to learn when repairs are scheduled and whether there is a backlog
